messages:
Maya Patel: Quick heads-up — planning a compact CRM curation sweep tonight (low-risk window 23:00-00:30 PT). Aim: remove obviously stale contacts, mark duplicates, and run healthscore recalculation after. Need volunteers for a dry-run and quick QA.
Ben Liu: I can take the dry-run. Do we have an exact deletion criteria? don't want to accidentally nuke active trials.
Maya Patel: Good Q. Proposed criteria:
```sql
-- candidate removals
WHERE last_seen < now() - interval '18 months'
AND account_stage NOT IN ('active_trial','poc')
AND contact_has_no_touchpoints = true
AND not_recent_revenue_flag
```
We will only tag records with `cs:prune-candidate` in the dry-run, no deletes.
Priya Desai: tagging only sounds safe. Can we also surface a list of accounts that would be affected so AMs can skim? Even 1 page export.
Carlos Mendez: I can build the export. Will add columns: account_name, owner, last_seen, last_touch, health_score_current.
Ben Liu: thanks. Also request: when we recalc healthscore, we should stash previous scores and run a delta check for any >10 point jumps.
Maya Patel: yes — recalc will emit a delta report. If any account jumps >10 pts we'll hold the change and create a review ticket.
Priya Desai: loop in Enablement to collect any manual feedback for borderline accounts (30-50 score) — I can ping them after the dry-run.
Carlos Mendez: schedule looks good. I'll run the tagging job at 23:05 PT and post the export in this thread. CS Ops Bot will run the sample report.
CS Ops Bot: automated-run scheduled: crm_tagging_dryrun @ 2026-03-23T23:05:00-07:00. Will post CSV preview and counts when done.
CS Ops Bot: DRYRUN RESULT: 1,124 contacts flagged as cs:prune-candidate across 312 accounts. Preview: <link to secure csv>
Maya Patel: awesome. Priya, Ben — can you review CSV by 08:00 PT tomorrow? If no objections we do live prune next Tuesday during low traffic window.
Ben Liu: reviewing now, will reply with any redlines. :thumbsup: 
Priya Desai: on it. I'll also brief Enablement to collect any discordant feedback. Thanks team!
